title: What Is The Biblical Remnant
paragraphs: The Biblical Remnant: A Study in God's Faithful Preservation

Throughout Scripture, the concept of the "remnant" appears as a powerful thread, weaving together the story of God’s faithfulness, judgment, and grace. But what does the Bible mean by “remnant," and why is it such an important theme? Let’s explore this concept, tracing its meaning from the Old Testament to its fulfillment in Christ and application for believers today.
1. The Remnant in the Old Testament

The term “remnant” refers to a group that survives or remains after a crisis, often as a result of God’s intervention. In the Old Testament, it typically points to those who remain faithful to God despite widespread unfaithfulness.
After Israel’s repeated disobedience, God warned of judgment but also promised that a remnant would remain:
Except Jehovah of hosts had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom, we should have been like unto Gomorrah. - Isaiah 1:9 ASV
Even when God allowed Israel and Judah to be taken into exile, He preserved a remnant to fulfill His promises:

And it shall come to pass in that day, that the remnant of Israel, and they that are escaped of the house of Jacob, shall no more again lean upon him that smote them, but shall lean upon Jehovah, the Holy One of Israel, in truth. - Isaiah 10:20 ASV
This remnant was not just about ethnic survival; it was about spiritual faithfulness—a people who continued to trust in the Lord.
2. The Remnant in the Prophets
The prophetic books frequently speak of a remnant who will return to God and be restored:
But in Mount Zion there shall be those that escape, and it shall be holy; and the house of Jacob shall possess their possessions. - Obadiah 1:17 ASV
The remnant theme assures God’s people that, even in judgment, God’s promises are not nullified. He preserves a people for Himself, ensuring the continuity of His redemptive plan.
3. The Remnant and the Coming Messiah
The prophets connected the remnant with the coming of the Messiah. The remnant would be the nucleus through which God’s salvation would reach all nations:

And the remnant that is escaped of the house of Judah shall again take root downward, and bear fruit upward. For out of Jerusalem shall go forth a remnant, and out of mount Zion they that shall escape: the zeal of Jehovah of hosts will perform this. - Isaiah 37:31-32 ASV
4. The Remnant in the New Testament

The New Testament picks up the remnant theme, showing its fulfillment in Christ. The Apostle Paul refers to the remnant to explain God’s continued faithfulness to Israel and to emphasize that salvation is always by grace:
Even so then at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace. - Romans 11:5 ASV
Paul makes clear that the remnant is not about ethnicity alone, but about faith in Jesus Christ. God’s saving work continues through those who trust in Him.
5. Theological Insights
God’s Sovereignty and Grace: The remnant exists because of God’s initiative and mercy, not human merit (Romans 9:27 ASV).
Faithfulness in Difficult Times: Throughout Scripture, the remnant is often a minority, reminding believers to remain faithful even when others turn away (2 Timothy 1:13 ASV).
The Universal Scope of Salvation: While the remnant began with Israel, God’s plan was always to include people from every nation who would believe in Christ (Galatians 3:28 ASV).
6. Application for Believers Today

The remnant encourages Christians to persevere in faith, trusting that God always preserves a people for Himself. Even in times of spiritual decline or opposition, God’s promises remain sure. Salvation is by grace through faith in Jesus Christ, and all who trust in Him are part of God’s faithful people.
For by grace have ye been saved through faith; and that not of yourselves, it is the gift of God. - Ephesians 2:8 ASV
Conclusion

The biblical remnant is a testament to God’s unwavering faithfulness. It reminds us that, no matter how dark the times or how small the number, God preserves His people, fulfills His promises, and invites all who believe in Christ to be part of His redeemed community.
